a_passing_gate_means: structural integrity of the declared artifacts

runtime.dependency_note: All 14 validate_*.py scripts import standard library only; validate_boundary_cases_v0_3.py, validate_corpus_application_v0_3.py, and validate_second_stratum.py import the sibling repo module validate_boundary_cases (not a PyPI package). No pinned third-party dependency is required.

registration_policy.rule: Every validate_*.py present in the repository root MUST appear in this manifest as a validator script. An unregistered validator causes gate failure; it is never silently ignored. Adding a new validator is therefore a deliberate governance act, not an automatic consequence of file discovery.

exclusion.reason: Pre-existing baseline-integrity defect on base 9a6b6f7. ASR_001_REVIEW_BASELINE_MANIFEST.json records sha256 values that do not match the committed content of five files (ASR_001_WORKING_DRAFT_V0.2.md, ASR_001_CLAUSE_TO_FIELD_MAP_V0.2.json, ASR_001_INTERNAL_TRIAL_RESULTS.md, ASR_001_CLAUSE_FRICTION_REGISTER_V0.1.json, ASR_001_INTERNAL_TRIAL_INDEX_V0.2.json). Worktree equals HEAD, so this is committed drift, not a checkout artifact.
exclusion.why_not_fixed_here: Re-attesting the ASR-001 review baseline is an owner governance action on ASR review material, outside the scope of establishing the CI gate and outside the governance boundaries set for this task. It is recorded as an open blocker rather than silently skipped or worked around.
exclusion.handling: The gate still RUNS this validator on every invocation and REPORTS its PASS/FAIL, so the defect stays visible. Its result does not fail the gate while required=false.
